title: Should You Buy Microsoft Stock Before the Huge Investor Update? | MSFT Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc previews Microsoft's earnings, due after the close on 28 October 2026, and answers whether to buy before the update. He owns the stock — added around $400 in February after a fall to near $350 — ranked it an excellent buying opportunity earlier this year, then downgraded it to a hold a couple of weeks ago (last evaluated 5 October) as the valuation richened; at $524 he reiterates that hold: not a seller, but not a buyer before the print either, because elevated event risk needs a higher prospective return. His updated discounted cash flow is $447 against the $524 price — slightly overvalued — while the forward P/E of 22.1 is below the stock's own average. The most recent quarter (reported 29 July) showed revenue of $90 billion, up 18% year over year, with the AI segment growing over 40%; his earnings-growth estimate of about 20% sits above the analyst figure, which drops out of the auto-captions. His watch list: Microsoft 365 paid seats (30 million stated), progress on its own chips, where it trails Alphabet and Amazon, a backlog approaching $500 billion (the unit drops out of the captions) and its OpenAI concentration, fiscal 2027 capex, and whether Microsoft stays the only hyperscaler that is free-cash-flow positive. The call is MSFT — HOLD reiterated.

calls.price_at_call: $524 (stated current); DCF fair value $447 (stated) — slightly overvalued on his DCF
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 5 Oct, after downgrading from an excellent-buying-opportunity ranking earlier this year; no flip) — he owns Microsoft (added around $400 in February, after a low near $350), is not interested in selling, and is also not interested in buying before the 28 Oct earnings release because at $524 the risk/reward does not compensate for print risk.
calls.base_case: Most recent reported quarter (29 Jul): revenue $90bn, up 18% year over year (the operating-income increase figure drops out of the captions); forward P/E 22.1, below the stock's own average on that metric; Microsoft's AI segment is growing over 40%.
calls.bull_case: He thinks analyst earnings growth forecasts (the figure drops out of the captions, around 15%) underestimate — he expects closer to 20% EPS growth; backlog approaching $500bn (unit drops out of the captions) and Microsoft may be the only hyperscaler free-cash-flow positive through fiscal 2027.
calls.bear_case: Backlog concentration in OpenAI is a key risk, its own-chip programme trails Alphabet and Amazon, AI investment has flattened operating leverage, and peers may fund the race with dilutive equity (he reads Meta's new share class that way).
